mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month does not correlate with negative 5-day forward returns in > 70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST drops > 10% in 1 month does not correlate with negative 60-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases do not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it indicates a potential economic recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the combination of UNRATE > 7% and FEDFUNDS < 1% does not correlate with positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in one month signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% in 1 month does not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real final sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases > 5% in 1 month does not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it indicates a tight labor market and potential inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the combination of UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS > 2% does not correlate with negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of triggered instances.
